text:
devin: thinking out loud — can we schedule proactive GPU card swaps into low-SLA maintenance windows when our health probe predicts a >70% chance of a catastrophic ECC/Xid in the next 72h?

(tl;dr: prefer short scheduled swap over emergency drain + replacement during peak, reduces preemption and cross-region capacity churn)

tanya: curious — how do you estimate the 72h window? model/heuristics or simple rate threshold?

devin: it's a fuzzy score from the health classifier: ECC burst frequency, rising Xid error rate, thermal jitter, and memtest retest failures. not perfect but gives us a short lead time. idea is to only auto-schedule a swap if score > 0.7 AND we can book a swap slot within the next maintenance window for that AZ.

kevin: will require a change to our drain flow. we currently do immediate cordon+drain for Xid spikes. scheduling means we mark node as 'swap_pending' and let it keep running until the window starts. that could impact jobs if it degrades quickly. risk.

ashok: agree risk exists. fallback: if instantaneous error rate crosses a hard threshold (e.g., Xid > 100/min OR GPU ECC fatal count > 5 in 10m) we still emergency-cordon. scheduled swaps only for predictive-but-not-yet-urgent nodes. also propose reserving a tiny warm spare pool per-AZ for scheduled swap windows so we don't oversubscribe.

sam: reserving spares has cost tradeoffs. what's the projected OPEX impact? even 5 spares across 3 AZs adds up.

devin: totally — preliminary calc: 5 N4g-p4 per-AZ warm spares ~ $X/day. but each scheduled swap avoids a forced replacement event which historically spikes cross-region replication and job resubmits increasing cost. need to model. I'll run numbers.

infra-bot: [alert] node gpu-az3-146 flagged by health-probe score=0.78, recent_xid=12/1h, ecc_nonfatal=3/24h. suggested action: schedule-swap window next low-SLA slot 2028-06-21T02:00Z -> 2028-06-21T04:00Z.

tanya: on the integration side, how will Slurm jobs behave? will we requeue or drain with REQUEUE? we should preserve long-running batch work.

kevin: recommend two-tier draining for scheduled swaps: 1) soft-evict with requeue for RQ-friendly jobs (MPI checkpoints) 2) for non-requeueable, annotate and schedule last-chance migration attempts. we can reuse slurm part of our current drain-orch but add a scheduled-delay param.

ashok: example flow sketch:
```
# mark node as pending swap
kubectl label node gpu-az3-146 infra/swap-pending=2028-06-21T02:00Z
# set taint for new scheduling policy but keep running until window
kubectl taint nodes gpu-az3-146 swap-window=true:NoSchedule --overwrite
```

sam: sounds fine, but we need guardrails in the console for users to opt-out if they have latency-sensitive workloads during a window. also need SLA notifications 24h/1h prior.

devin: agreed. ops-oncall, can you own the initial runbook and notification text? I can handle the metrics and simulation.

ops-oncall: yep. I'll draft a short runbook: detection -> schedule -> reserve spare -> notify owners -> staged-drain -> post-swap health checks -> untaint. will share in #oncall-runbooks.

tanya: rollout plan proposal: 1) simulation on historical traces (2 weeks) 2) enable in canary AZ (az1) with 1 spare kept 3) monitor job impact & tail latency for 2 weeks 4) expand.

devin: thanks. I'll run the sim and post results. one more: we should add a small hysteresis window so nodes with transient blips don't get scheduled. e.g., require sustained score>0.7 for 3 consecutive probes (probe cadence = 2h).

infra-bot: note: emergency-cordon threshold configured at xid_rate>200/min or ecc_fatal>1/10m. scheduled-swap rules will not override that.

kevin: one implementation detail — add a new DB column node_swap_window and existing drain-orch will read it. also add metric 'swap_scheduled' for billing visibility.

sam: ok to proceed with simulation. please include a cost delta table in the report.

devin: will do. action items: devin -> simulate & cost model (ETA 3d), ops-oncall -> draft runbook & notifications (ETA 2d), kevin -> spec DB + drain-orch read (ETA 5d), tanya -> slurm requeue policy mapping (ETA 4d).

ashok: add me to the PR review for orchestration changes.

devin: thanks all :pray: we'll iterate after simulation.
